intro: Sarajevo rewards visitors who wander without a fixed plan. Its old bazaar, riverside walks and war-era history reveal more the longer you stay. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Currency is the Bosnian convertible mark (KM), not USD. Prices below are in KM unless noted.
Trams and trolleybuses run the city. Tram 3 runs the full line from Ilidža to the centre. Tram 1 and 4 serve the central loop. There is no metro.

Single tram, trolleybus or bus ticket costs 2.20 KM. Day ticket is 7.10 KM. Buy in the Javni prevoz KS app, from drivers, or at GRAS kiosks. Bus tickets are bought from the driver, and pre-bought tram tickets are not valid on buses.

Taxis are the main scam risk. Legitimate taxis have a TAXI sign and plates with TA. Insist on the meter and ask for a receipt. Official firms include Paja 1522, Žuti 033 66 35 55 and Samir & Emir 1516.
Driving is not recommended in the Old Town, where streets are steep, narrow and one-way. Parking is very hard to find.

Walking is the best way to see the centre. Street signs are scarce, so use a map app. Nextbike rental has about 14 stations along the tram lines, with 30 free minutes per day and 1.50 KM after that. Separate bike lanes run along the river and main boulevard for over 5 km.
No ferry service operates in the city.

bascarsija.name: Baščaršija
bascarsija.hours: Open all day · shops usually 09:00–20:00 (check on the day)
bascarsija.tip: Start here: walk the cobbled lanes of the old Ottoman bazaar and stop for coffee in a copper-pot café.

latin_bridge.name: Latin Bridge
latin_bridge.tip: This small bridge is where Archduke Franz Ferdinand was shot in 1914; a plaque marks the spot.

gazi_husrev_mosque.name: Gazi Husrev-bey Mosque
gazi_husrev_mosque.hours: Daily, around prayer times · check on the day, closed to visitors during prayers
gazi_husrev_mosque.tip: Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes at the door, and ask staff before taking photos inside.

tunnel_museum.name: Sarajevo Tunnel Museum (Tunnel of Hope)
tunnel_museum.price_text: About 5 USD (estimate) · check on the day
tunnel_museum.hours: Daily, roughly 09:00–18:00 · check on the day
tunnel_museum.tip: Take a taxi or tram ride out to Butmir; the 800 m tunnel under the airport was a lifeline during the siege.

city_hall.name: Sarajevo City Hall (Vijećnica)
city_hall.price_text: Exterior free · interior fees vary (check on the day)
city_hall.hours: Exterior always visible · interior hours vary, check on the day
city_hall.tip: The Moorish-style building was burned in 1992 and rebuilt; photograph the façade from the riverbank.

eternal_flame.name: Eternal Flame
eternal_flame.tip: A memorial flame for the Sarajevo siege; it is a quiet stop between the old town and the river.

cevapi.name: Ćevapi
cevapi.hours: Most grills open around 10:00–22:00 · check on the day
cevapi.tip: Order a plate of grilled minced-meat sausages with somun bread and raw onion, the local staple.

markale_market.name: Markale Market
markale_market.price_text: Free to walk · food costs vary
markale_market.tip: Go early for fresh produce, cheese and local bread, and watch your bag in the crowds.

yellow_bastion.name: Yellow Bastion (Žuta tabija)
yellow_bastion.tip: Climb the Ottoman-era fortification in the old town for the best view over the red roofs at sunset.

vratnik_walk.name: Vratnik old-town walk
vratnik_walk.price_text: Free self-guided · guided tours about 15–30 USD (estimate)
vratnik_walk.tip: Wander the steep Vratnik lanes above Baščaršija for quiet streets, old houses and city views.

trebevic_cable_car.name: Trebević cable car
trebevic_cable_car.price_text: About 15–25 USD return (estimate) · check on the day
trebevic_cable_car.hours: Usually daily, roughly 09:00–18:00 · check on the day; may be closed in bad weather
trebevic_cable_car.tip: Ride up for hiking trails and city views, then see the bobsled track ruins on the mountain.

walking_tour_city.name: Free walking tour of Sarajevo
walking_tour_city.hours: Daily, usually morning and afternoon slots · check on the day
walking_tour_city.tip: Tip your guide at the end; a good tour covers the siege history and the bazaar in about 2 to 3 hours.

stays.why: Walk to the bazaar, Sebilj and most old-town sights. Quiet at night, and narrow streets mean you walk rather than drive.
Near the main boulevard and the river bike lanes. Trams 1, 3 and 4 serve the centre, so reaching the old town is easy.
Central and walkable, with many cafés and shops. Good base for trams and the Nextbike stations along the tram lines.
Quiet residential old-town edge below the fortress. Lovely views, but steep streets and no driving, so pack light.

food: Try ćevapi (grilled minced meat rolls) in Baščaršija, usually served with raw onion and somun bread.
Order burek or sirnica (pastry with meat or cheese) for breakfast, then finish with baklava and Bosnian coffee in a copper pot.
Eat at the bazaar cafés and kebab grills around Baščaršija. Prices are in KM, so check the menu before ordering.
Sit in a traditional kafana for slow coffee and local dishes. Book ahead on weekends if you can.
Pay in KM. Carry some small notes and coins for kiosks and buses, since bus tickets are bought from the driver.
more_time: Take a day trip to Mostar for the old bridge and the old town. Check bus times on the day.
Ride Tram 3 to Ilidža for the spa park and gardens, at the far end of the full line.
Go up Trebević or Jahorina for views over the city and the mountains. Check the transport and weather on the day.
